query: What review signals predict negative IMDb audience satisfaction?

per_column.name: negative_word_count
per_column.rationale: Count of negative-sentiment words in the review text; lies outside the label, is knowable before the outcome, and plausibly carries strong signal about negative satisfaction. A legitimate lexical predictor.

per_column.name: exclamation_count
per_column.rationale: Punctuation-based intensity feature derived from text, independent of the label. Weak-to-moderate but plausible signal (emotional emphasis can associate with polarity), not leakage or restatement.

per_column.name: caps_word_count
per_column.rationale: All-caps word count captures emphasis/shouting, a stylistic cue that can correlate with strong (often negative) sentiment. Outside the focus and non-leaky; modest predictive value.

per_column.name: negation_intensifier_count
per_column.rationale: Counts negations/intensifiers, which modulate sentiment polarity and intensity; a legitimate text-derived predictor that plausibly helps distinguish negative reviews without restating the label.

judge.rationale: All four columns are text-derived features that lie outside the focus variable, are knowable prior to the outcome (no leakage), and none restate label_pos. negative_word_count is the strongest signal for the negative-satisfaction target; negation_intensifier_count adds polarity-modulating signal; exclamation_count and caps_word_count contribute weaker stylistic emphasis cues. As a set they give moderate genuine predictive leverage beyond review_text alone, though they are relatively generic lexical/stylistic counts rather than richly engineered semantic features, capping their utility.
